interest: Index of Diet sessions in the 1930s, from Shidehara to Ozaki's 1937 interpellation.
overview: This file consists of the Department of State's nine-page 'List of Papers' (docket sheet register) for decimal classification 894.032, recording documents received and filed between January 1930 and January 1938 concerning the proceedings, legislative actions, and major policy addresses of the Japanese Imperial Diet. The register indexes incoming telegrams, despatches, cross-reference sheets, and memoranda primarily submitted to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs by U.S. Embassy officials in Tokyo (including Ambassadors William R. Castle, Jr., W. Cameron Forbes, and Joseph C. Grew, and Chargé Edwin L. Neville), along with reports from diplomatic and consular posts in Peiping, Nanking, Shanghai, Tsingtao, London, and Moscow, and texts furnished by the Japanese Embassy in Washington. Key subjects tracked include annual policy statements by Japanese Prime Ministers and Foreign Ministers (notably Kijuro Shidehara, Makoto Saito, Yasuya Uchida, and Koki Hirota), debates over emergency military appropriations and relief programs, Diet dissolutions and national elections, diplomatic fallout from the creation of Manchukuo, and significant parliamentary interpellations by lawmakers such as Yukio Ozaki and Seigo Nakano.

subfiles.about: A nine-page Department of State docket sheet register indexing incoming and outgoing documents, cross-reference sheets, and memoranda filed under decimal classification 894.032 concerning proceedings of the Japanese Imperial Diet from 1930 through 1938.
subfiles.summary: This nine-page Department of State 'List of Papers' catalogs documents 89 through 179 under decimal file 894.032, recording diplomatic correspondence and internal memoranda on the Japanese Imperial Diet between January 1930 and January 1938. The register indexes reporting from U.S. diplomatic missions in Tokyo, Peiping, Nanking, Shanghai, Tsingtao, London, and Moscow, as well as policy addresses provided directly by the Japanese Embassy in Washington. Major topics covered include annual opening addresses by Prime Ministers and Foreign Ministers (Shidehara, Saito, Uchida, and Hirota), debates over emergency military appropriations and relief programs, Diet dissolutions and national elections, diplomatic fallout from the creation and recognition of Manchukuo, political developments following the February 26 Incident of 1936, and prominent parliamentary interpellations by figures such as Yukio Ozaki and Seigo Nakano.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: File 894.032 – Proceedings of the Japanese Diet (1930–1938)
